title: Weekly attendance exports for community arts courses
beneficiary: Course coordinators and instructors at eight independent community arts centers using a shared hosted administration service.
valued_outcome: Coordinators receive usable attendance files for the intended courses and week, with little manual work and no records from another center.
success_measure: Across the next 40 weekly exports, median coordinator handling time is at most 12 minutes, at least 95% contain the intended course set, and none contain another center’s participant records.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: Participant names must remain inside the existing private service and each center’s authorized workspace; no public external processing service may receive them.
The centers’ current spreadsheet import accepts one documented CSV schema, which must continue to be supported for the coming term.
A first bounded change has at most six engineer-days and must fit the existing monthly hosting allowance.
Instructors must remain able to enter attendance during ordinary class hours, including the interval when exports are prepared.

changeable_assumptions: Exports run on Sunday evening because that was the schedule requested by the first center.
The service treats a course’s current instructor assignment as the assignment relevant to any requested week.
incumbent_description: A scheduled job produces a CSV per center. A coordinator downloads it Monday, compares course names with a local schedule, and requests another export when something appears absent.

supplied_observations.text: In a sample of 40 exports, 32 contained the intended course set; eight prompted additional handling before coordinators used them.
Median handling time across all 40 files was 17 minutes. For 24 files from centers with unchanged course assignments, the median was seven minutes.
Six of the eight affected exports concerned courses whose instructor assignment changed during the requested week; two concerned recently renamed courses.
No cross-center rows were found in the 40 sampled files. This sample did not include the center that recently split one course into two.
Job execution took 40 to 75 seconds. Coordinators waited between 20 minutes and two working days for requested replacement files.
Four coordinators maintain separate schedules; three use the service’s course list; one keeps a printed timetable annotated during the week.
Service logs record job completion and row totals, but the sample includes no recordings of coordinator actions inside their spreadsheet application.

unmeasured_variables: The completeness and update timing of each local timetable.
Handling time attributable to checking, correcting, downloading, and importing separately.
available_resources: One engineer, a staging copy containing fabricated participants, and six consenting coordinators for two short sessions each.
Existing export logs and the documented CSV format.
evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data
